newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise gasoline prices Thurs - Arrieta.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise gasoline prices Thurs - Arrieta.

text.p: An increase in Venezuela's gasoline prices will go into effect Thursday, Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said.
"It goes into effect on July 17," Arrieta told reporters after making a presentation at an investors' forum.

Arrieta later confirmed that low-grade fuel would increase 20 percent to 60 bolivars ($0.12), medium-grade fuel would increase 27 percent to 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter, and high-grade fuel will rise 33 percent to 80 bolivars ($0.16) per liter.
"It's a rational increase which makes sense and won't have a negative impact on the economy," Arrieta said.
Under a stand-by loan agreement signed with the International Monetary Fund last July, the government hiked gasoline prices 500 percent and pledged to increase them toward market levels.

The free on board (FOB) export price of Venezuelan premium unleaded gasoline Monday was about $0.155 per liter, and it is the government's intention to move domestic prices closer to that market level.
Arrieta added that diesel prices would not be raised.
Gasoline prices have been a sensitive issue in Venezuela since hundreds died in 1989 riots following a price hike.
